sentences: Credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 27% of the model's importance, and risk rises strongly as utilization climbs.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with a moderate to strong effect, and risk jumps once an applicant has at least one delinquency.
The effect of credit utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies: utilization adds much more risk for applicants who have delinquencies than for those who have none.
Income is the third or fourth most important driver, with a moderate effect, and risk falls as income rises.
The length of credit history is also a third or fourth most important driver with a moderate effect, and risk falls as the history gets longer; this matters more than the debt-to-income ratio.
The debt-to-income ratio is the fifth most important driver, with a weak to moderate effect, and risk rises with it, though it matters less than the length of credit history.
Age and months at the current address hardly matter for default risk, and the number of dependents has at most a weak effect.

Credit utilization does not interact with income or with the length of credit history, and the number of past delinquencies does not interact with income; the data do not settle whether the length of credit history and recent inquiries interact.
